course_description:
This course will introduce biomechanical principles and how they relate to the analysis of human movement to help understand human performance, potential mechanisms of injury and understanding how to prevent injuries and how the body interacts with the environment or equipment. The course will cover the interaction of the human body with the physical world by combining principles from biology and physics - kinematics, kinetics, energetics and muscle function. It will provide students with skills for quantitative and qualitative analysis of human movement, which can be applied in the context of health, exercise, sport and activities of daily living in a variety of populations.

Biomechanics covers the application of the principles of mechanics to the study of biological systems. The course will cover the interaction of the human body with the physical world by combining principles from biology and physics.

learning_outcomes.description: Describe biomechanical principles and how they relate specifically to the analysis of human movement
Perform biomechanical calculations to quantify human movement performance
Conduct a biomechanical analysis of human movement using a variety of instruments
Analyse, interpret and communicate biomechanical data for both performance enhancement and injury prevention in health and disease.
Work effectively within a team in order to develop appropriate biomechanical analysis and communication skills, and facilitate peer-assisted, collaborative learning.

assessment_details.title: Video Analysis Assignment
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment requires students to apply biomechanical concepts and methods to the analysis of human movement. Working collaboratively in groups, students will collect, process, analyse and interpret biomechanical data from a movement task. The assessment is designed to develop skills in movement analysis, critical interpretation of biomechanical evidence, and communication of findings to a relevant audience. Groups will be required to identify the purpose of their analysis and select appropriate biomechanical variables, principles and methods to address their chosen movement question. Using digital tools and biomechanical analysis techniques, students will collect and evaluate movement data, interpret the findings in relation to biomechanical theory and relevant evidence, and consider the implications for performance, injury prevention, rehabilitation, training or movement optimisation. The outcomes of the project will be communicated through a group video presentation. The presentation should demonstrate the group's ability to: define a clear aim and rationale for the biomechanical analysis; collect and analyse movement data using appropriate biomechanical methods and technologies; apply anatomical and biomechanical principles to interpret findings; communicate key outcomes using appropriate visualisations and supporting evidence; provide informed recommendations, practical applications, or future directions based on the analysis. Students are expected to work collaboratively throughout the project using university-supported digital collaboration tools. Use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their video submission independent of AI and MT tools. These issues should be actively managed by the group and the Course Coordinator as appropriate, during semester.

learning_activities.topic: Introduction online laboratory Course introduction and information. View introductory videos and contribute to introductory tasks Learning outcomes: L01
Introduction to Biomechanics Biomechanics, Describing and Quantifying Motion Learning outcomes: L01
Linear Kinematics Displacement, Velocity and Acceleration, Uniform accelerated motion and projectiles Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Kinematics laboratory Kinematics Lab. Measuring split times while running or walking over a track instrumented with timing lights. Determine average and instantaneous velocities from collected data. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Linear Kinetics Newton's Laws, Force and Acceleration, Different Types of Forces Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Collisions and Impact Impulse - Momentum, Collisions, Walking and Running forces Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Vertical jump laboratory Measure ground reaction forces and impulse during jumping to determine jump performance with different techniques Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Work, Power and Energy Mechanical Work, Mechanical Power, Energy Learning outcomes: L01, L02

Torque and Power laboratory Measure how sit-up techniques influences lever arm, muscle force, joint reaction force and effort. Measure arm muscle power during an upright row lift and determine the effect of load. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Rotational Forces Torque and Moment Arms, Torque and Muscle Force, Centre of Gravity and Stability Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Angular Kinematics Angular Kinematics, Analysing Angular Kinematics Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Angular Kinematics laboratory Measure angular kinematics using OpenCap to determine the influence of different techniques on performance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Angular Kinetics Moment of Inertia, Angular Kinetics Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Human Movement Analysis Movement Analysis, Technical Considerations of Video Analysis Learning outcomes: L01, L02
Muscle and strength Muscle architecture, Dynamic force constraints, Neural activation Learning outcomes: L01, L02
